WPMS No. 794 of 2009 
U. C. Dhyani, J.
Mr. A.K. Sharma, Advocate for the writ 
petitioner. 
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Standing Counsel for the 
State/respondent no. 5. 
None is present for the other respondents. 
Stay application has been filed by the petitioner 
for directing the parties to maintain status quo. 
List the petition for final hearing in the month of 
July, 2016. 
Considering the facts of the case, it is provided, as 
an interim measure that, status quo on the land in 
question shall be maintained by the parties till the next 
date of listing. 
CLMA Nos. 4284/2009 and 5337/2016 stand 
disposed of.

Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. A.K. Sharma, Advocate for the 
petitioner. 
Mr. Suyash Pant, Standing Counsel for the 
State of Uttarakhand.

counter affidavit within the aforesaid period. 
List after three weeks.

date of listing.

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
WPMS No. 794 of 2009
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Tapan Singh, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. M.S. Bisht, learned Brief Holder for the 
State/respondent no. 5.
3. No representation for respondent nos. 2 and 3 
despite service.
4. In the previous order dated 18.03.2021, learned 
counsel for the petitioner was directed to serve the 
copy of the writ petition to the counsel for the Gram 
Sabha within 48 hours. It has been informed by the 
State Counsel that Mrs. Anjali Bhargawa is the 
Standing Counsel for the Gram Sabha; however, her 
name is not shown in the cause list.
5. Learned Brief Holder Mr. M.S. Bisht for the 
State is directed to file an affidavit bringing on record 
the report of Lekhpal as well as the proposal of the 
Gram Sabha, on the basis of which the lease was 
granted to respondent no. 3 under the provisions of 
U.P.Z.A. & L.R. Act, 1950. Learned Brief Holder 
may also bring on record all the relevant documents 
including the copy of lease.
6. It is made clear that since this matter is very 
old one pending since 2009 and, therefore, this matter 
will not be adjourned.
7. List this matter on 16.06.2023 by showing the 
name of Mrs. Anjali Bhargawa as a counsel for Gram 
Sabha.
8. Interim order dated 06.06.2016 will continue to 
operate till 16.06.2023.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 22.05.2023

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS 
16.06.2023 WPMS No. 794 of 2009 
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
 
1. Mr. Tapan Singh, learned counsel for the 
petitioner. 
2. Ms. Anjali Bhargawa, learned counsel for 
respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 4. 
3. Mr. Pradeep Hairia, learned Standing Counsel 
with Mr. Mohinder Singh Bisht, learned Brief Holder for 
the State of Uttarakhand / respondent No. 5. 
4. By order dated 04.06.2009, notices were issued 
to respondent Nos. 1 to 4 and, thereafter, steps were 
taken. 
5. The Office report dated 10.08.2010 indicates that 
the notice was issued to respondent No. 3 through 
registered post on 18.03.2010 returnable before 
19.04.2010, and this report further indicates that 30 
days’ time has passed since no undelivered envelop 
returned back, therefore, service is sufficient. 
6. Service has been effected upon respondent No. 
3, as per the office report dated 10.08.2010, despite 
this, respondent No. 3 has not put his presence himself 
or through his counsel in the proceedings of the present 
writ petition.  7. This petition has been filed by the petitioner, who 
has purchased the property from respondent No. 3 
while the proceedings were pending in the Court of the 
Assistant Collector. 
8. Today Ms. Shalini Maurya, Tehsildar, Tehsil￾Roorkee is present in the Court with the original record, 
and the counsel placed before me an Application moved 
by the Pradhan and Member, Gram Sabha Bharapur, 
Bhauri Pargana and Tehsil Roorkee, District Haridwar 
dated 25.09.2003, wherein there is an endorsement 
made by the Collector on 25.09.2003, which reads as 
under:- 
 “oknh ds vf/koDrk dks lquk x;kA [kljk ua 133@5 Jh eku th] dks fodz; 
fd;s tkus gsrq i{kksa dk s fuf"k) fd;k tkrk gSA” 
9. As per that endorsement of the Collector dated 
25.09.2003, there was prohibition to sell the land 
falling in Khasra No. 133/5. 
10. The State Counsel further submits that the 
petitioner purchased the land of the same Khasra 
Number through Sale Deed dated 30.10.2003, though 
the Collector restrained to sell the land falling in Khasra 
No. 133/5. 
11. Since there is no counter-affidavit on behalf of  the respondents, all these aspects are required to be 
scrutinized. Hence, the State Counsel is directed to file 
a comprehensive counter-affidavit bringing on record 
all the relevant documents within a period of two 
weeks. 
12. Ms. Anjali Bhargawa, learned counsel for 
respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3, also wishes to file a 
counter affidavit. She seeks two weeks’ time to do so. 
The time, so prayed for, is granted. 
13. The petitioner may file his rejoinder-affidavit(s) 
within a period of one week thereafter. 
14. The interim order passed by this Court dated 
06.06.2016 is modified to the extent that the petitioner 
will not create any third party interest in respect of the 
property-in-question till further orders. 
15. List on 07.07.2023. No further adjournment 
shall be granted to either of the parties. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J) 
 16.06.2023 
Rathour

WPSS No. 722 of 2023 
And 
WPSS No. 783 of 2023 
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. M. C. Pant, Ms. Prabha Naithani, 
and Mr. K.K. Joshi learned counsel appear 
for the petitioners. 
2. Mr. Yashpal Arya, learned counsel 
holding brief of Mr. Neeraj Garg, learned 
counsel for the UPNL. 
3. Mr. Pradeep Hariya, learned Standing 
Counsel for the State. 
4. In all these writ petitions, the 
petitioners are serving in different 
departments, who were engaged through 
UPNL.
5. According to the petitioners, they are 
working for last more than 10 years.
6. In Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1089 of 2023, 
the relief is being sought that the State may 
frame a scheme for the employees, who are 
serving through UPNL for last more than 10  years. 
7. Almost, in all the writ petitions, 
identical issues are being raised and main 
grievance of the petitioners in all these Writ 
Petitions is that they are serving for last more 
than 10 years through UPNL. 
8. The State has already filed, in some of 
the writ petitions, its counter affidavits, 
however, in Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1089 of 
2023, counter affidavit has not been filed. 
9. Mr. Pradeep Hairiya who represents the
State, seeks two weeks’ time to file a counter 
affidavit in Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1089 of 
2023, because in this Writ Petition, a relief is 
being sought for framing a scheme of 
absorption. 
10. Let the counter affidavit be filed in Writ 
Petition (S/S) No. 1089 of 2023, within a 
period of four weeks. 
11. Mr. Pradeep Hairiya further submits 
that on the next date, learned Advocate 
General will represent the State in these 
cases. 
12. List these matters on 25th August, 
2023. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 28.07.2023 Kaushal
